title: How to Test Ad Creatives on a Small Budget | AIVideosUGC
description: An ad creative is the video or photo in your ad. Test a few versions together from one photo, change one thing at a time, and read the results.
h1: How to Test Ad Creatives Without Guessing
lead: Here is how to test ad creatives. Change one thing at a time, so you learn which opening people actually watch. For these trail shoes, that one thing might be the first second: the two colorways side by side, or the shoes on a runner's feet. Run those files together.
secondary_keywords: ad creative testing for small business
summary: You find a winning opening for the trail shoes without a second filming day. Change one thing, and run a few versions on the same audience and budget.

paras: You can compare openings because the photo, the length, and the shape stay the same. Change only how the clip starts.

Photo ads work the same way, with the same clock and the same line. When the only change is the AI actor or the tone, ask for that and keep the clock. sections.h2: How Shops Set Up One Test
paras: A trail-shoe shop runs three openings of the same pair, and only the first second changes. The colorways stay the colorways in the photo.
A running shop makes one clip from the shoe photo, and the street in that photo stays the street. They do not build a second set.
A gift shop shows the shoes on a runner's feet in one file and side by side in the next. The pair itself does not change.

A second-market shop changes the spoken language, and the shoes stay the same. The script names only what the page says. The presenter speaks a line the shop wrote. An API can repeat that note when a new pair arrives.

sections.h2: How to Keep a Small Test Fair
paras: Change only one thing between clock versions, so the result points at that one thing.
Worth testing, one at a time: the opening moment, the setting, the shape, the length, and the line you add afterward. Start with the opening. It decides whether anyone sees the rest of the clock.

sections.h2: How the Versions Should Run Together
paras: One campaign gives every clock version the same audience, the same budget, and the same product page.

Many ad accounts let several ads share one group. Some also offer a built-in test that shows each version to part of the audience. The account may spend more on one version early. A version that barely ran has not been tested. Leave the ads as they are while the test is live, so the account keeps counting the same clock test.
sections.alt: Adult hands hold the same plain round wall clock in two matched side-by-side positions.

sections.h2: How to Tell Which Version Works
paras: Wait several days, until each clock version has actually played, before you name a winner.

Read three numbers in order. First, how many people stay past the opening. That tells you if the start works. Second, how often people click. That tells you if they wanted to visit. Third, the cost each time someone buys, or adds the clock to the cart. That matters most for the shop. A version can get more views and still lose on sales. If the numbers are close, that change did not matter much. Keep the one you prefer and test a bigger difference next.
sections.alt: Hands rest beside blank color cards and the same plain round wall clock.

sections.h2: What the Next Test Should Change
paras: You keep the clock version that brings sales at a cost you can accept, turn off the clear losers, and change one new thing.

Write down the date, what changed, and the result. After a few rounds you will see what your buyers respond to. When a winner starts costing more per sale, make fresh versions of the clock. Work through the opening, the setting, the shape, the length, then the offer. Each round starts from what already worked.

faq.q: What is a video ad you can test?
faq.a: A short paid-ad file of a product you already sell. For the trail shoes, you bring the photo, and you name the first second. The crew stays off the calendar for that test.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad to test?
faq.a: Upload the trail-shoe photo and write the first second you want, such as the two colorways coming into view. Download the shape this test uses.

faq.q: What should I look for when I pick a tool for ad tests?
faq.a: You want a second opening of the same trail shoes without a new photo shoot. The useful tool is the one that can make that second opening from the photo you have.

faq.q: Do I pay to make each version?
faq.a: Yes. A clip is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark. It can run as a paid placement and sit on the product page. You can run it without a separate permission form.

faq.q: Which frames can I download, and where can they run?
faq.a: Use 9:16 when the test runs on a phone screen, 1:1 when it sits in a feed, and 16:9 when the screen is wide. 4:3 and 3:4 are only for a placement that lists them. A second shape is a different test.

faq.q: Can I test ads for multiple products at once?
faq.a: Yes, if each pair of trail shoes has its own photo. Reuse one opening as the note, and let an API start a file when a new pair arrives. Many pairs still means one file each.

faq.q: Should I stop filming with people I hire?
faq.a: No. Keep a filmed spot when you want a person you hired on camera. Use a generated file when you are still choosing the first second. They answer different questions.

faq.q: Can a generated ad be turned down by the ad account?
faq.a: It can, for the same reasons any ad can. If the line sounds like a customer wrote a review, say so the way that app currently asks you to. Rules change, so read them before you raise the budget.

faq.q: How many versions should a small shop run?
faq.a: Start with a few, often three. More than that splits a small budget so far that no version gets a fair chance to play. Every extra version is another file.
The opening. It decides whether anyone watches the rest. Keep the shoes, the length, and the shape the same until that result is clear.

faq.q: Can I change the price on only one version?
faq.a: No. While you are testing the video or the photo, put the same words, the same price, and the same music on every file. Test the offer in a later round, on its own.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: From the ad account, after each version has played. The test does not invent a winner. You read who stayed, who clicked, and what a sale cost.

faq.q: What if the ad account barely shows one version?
faq.a: That version was not tested. Wait until each file has had a real chance to play, or the comparison is noise.

faq.q: Do I have to say the presenter is generated?
faq.a: Yes, when the ad could be read as a real customer's review. Follow that platform's disclosure rule. Give the AI actor a name you chose for the shop.
